title: Q2D conformance vector (authored form)
description: The authored vector, carrying both halves. P-001 §4.4 defines the format; this schema is its machine-checkable statement. The input-only projection a runner receives is P-001 §4.2 and P-001 issue 2 — implementations never see a file matching this schema.

id.description: Stable identifier, lowercase kebab segments separated by '/'. The first segment repeats 'section'; the harness checks the two agree and that the file sits under a directory of that name.

section.description: Corpus section. Closed, and extended additively by the PRD that owns the new section — the same discipline P-001 §4.5 applies to the operation vocabulary, and for the same reason: a typo must not create a section.

requirement.description: What this vector exercises. Mandatory with no default: P-001 §4.4 makes it what turns the corpus into a live traceability matrix, and a vector citing nothing is rejected by the linter. Each entry is a claim identifier from spec/claims.md, a conformance class from spec/conformance-classes.md, or a 'file.md#section' citation into spec/ or threat-model/. The harness checks that every entry resolves, including that the cited section exists and not merely the file.

description.description: One sentence, for the reader deciding whether the vector says what it claims to. A vector nobody can review is a vector nobody can trust.

operation.description: From the closed vocabulary in P-001 §4.5. Stages 5-8 extend this list, as one coordinated change, under P-001 issue 17 — the names anticipated there are proposals, not decisions, so they are deliberately absent here. An operation a runner does not recognise is exit 1, never a skip.

input.description: Everything the operation needs, including every value that would otherwise vary: keys, nonces, issued_at, expires_at, identifiers. P-001 §4.3 — a runner that reads a clock or generates a nonce is non-conforming.

expect.description: What a conforming implementation produces. The harness strips this before writing the file a runner reads (P-001 §4.2). Only 'ok' and 'rejected' may be expected: 'error' is a runner-reported outcome (P-001 §6) meaning the runner faulted, and an internal error is never a passing result.

output.description: Any JSON value. Its shape is the operation's, not this schema's.

comparison.description: 'bytes' where the spec requires determinism, 'semantic' where it does not. Stated per vector with no default, because a silent default is how a determinism requirement gets quietly dropped (P-001 §4.4). 'semantic' is parse-then-deep-equal and applies to unsigned material only; anything inside 'signed' compares as bytes.

oneOf.description: The implementation rejects the input. A successful run that reports a rejection, never a runner failure (P-001 §4.1).

rejection.description: Both halves, because the harness checks both (P-001 §4.6). The internal reason is what an implementation records locally; the wire response is what a requester receives.

wire.description:
What a requester receives. For a denial that is core-model.md §5.2's response object — status, external_reason, receipt, signature — where the receipt is the reduced shape §6 defines, exactly five fields.

A vector MAY assert a subset of those fields where response construction is not what it tests: a registry/ vector exercises whether a predicate evaluates and rejects correctly, and the envelope around the rejection is not its subject. A vector asserting a subset asserts nothing about the fields it omits, and `harness lint` names every partial comparison so that is visible rather than assumed.

denial/ may not, and lint rejects one that tries. Uniformity over part of a response is not uniformity: status and external_reason are both fixed by the normalized class, so a vector asserting only those compares two constants across every cause and cannot fail. §5.3 says where the leak actually hides — 'a receipt that recorded escalate for an outcome the wire made uniform would defeat Q2D-C-08 through the evidence attached to it, in the one place nobody looks for a normalization leak'. It is a lint rule rather than a schema one because it is conditional on the section, which this schema does not otherwise branch on.

A receipt a vector does assert is held to §6's shape exactly — five fields, no more and no fewer. Omitting receipt entirely asserts nothing about it; asserting a four- or six-field one asserts that a conforming implementation emits it, and §6 says none does.

No denial/ vector exists in the corpus yet, and one open question in P-001 §10 still decides bytes such a vector would carry: which RFC 3339 spelling a receipt timestamp uses. Authoring one first would settle it by example, in the section whose whole purpose is demonstrating Q2D-C-08. The other two blockers are gone: crypto-suites.md §3 defines the protected header, so a signature is producible, and §5.2's field list is closed at four, so an extra field is a lint failure rather than a question.

step.description: The core-model.md §4 step at which rejection occurred. Optional in general, and how the ordering/ section asserts ordering without instrumenting the implementation. An integer for a numbered step, or one of the lettered steps §4's table defines -- today only 9a, the rate-limit check. Closed rather than patterned, for the reason the operation vocabulary is closed: a vector citing step 12b would otherwise assert an ordering the specification does not have.

comparison.description: As above. A normalized denial compares as bytes: P-001 §4.8's cross-vector assertion needs the wire response to be byte-identical across causes.
